extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students and researchers in enumerative combinatorics
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques for counting combinatorial objects by representing them as walks in a weighted digraph (transfer-matrix method) or by factoring words in a free monoid (factorization method), and deriving rational generating functions and recurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer-matrix method (walks on a digraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the combinatorial objects as walks in a digraph D with a weight function w(e); let A be the adjacency matrix (with weights). Then the ordinary generating function for the number of walks (or for entries of An) is a rational function whose denominator is Q(λ) = det(I − λA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct vertices so that walks correspond bijectively to the combinatorial structures; set w(e)=1 for unweighted counts or appropriate weight monomials otherwise. Use the adjacency matrix A and compute Q(λ)=det(I−λA) to obtain rational generating functions (examples: several concrete enumerations in §4.7). Note: the method can lead to large matrices for complex dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarge state space to encode memory/history
rubrics_metrics.description: If allowed values at step i depend on more than the previous value ai−1, enlarge the digraph D so vertices encode the required past history (e.g., take V = [3]^2 with edges (ab, bc) if abc is allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the digraph 'big enough to incorporate the required past history' so that local transitions capture the global constraints. This trick converts higher-order dependencies into first-order transitions on tuples (examples: Example 4.7.7 and 4.7.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating function for closed walks / cyclic objects
rubrics_metrics.description: For counts of closed walks (cyclic / circular sequences), the generating function relates to the characteristic polynomial Q(λ) via expressions involving λ Q'(λ)/Q(λ) (summing traces/closed-walk contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closed-walk (cyclic) counts g(n) may be obtained from Q(λ) (determinant of I−λA) using the standard trace/logarithmic relations (examples yield formulas producing Lucas numbers, etc.). Be aware of "spurious" small-n values: for small n the combinatorial interpretation may fail and must be interpreted separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use initial values when numerator degree requires it
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing the full rational generating function from (I − λA)^{-1}, one may need a finite number of initial values to determine the numerator polynomial (degree bounded by results like Theorem 4.7.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of fully computing the characteristic polynomial and matrix inverse explicitly, compute a bounded set of initial coefficients f(0), f(1), … to determine the numerator; this is often much easier in practice (illustrated in examples computing Fibonacci numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization in free monoids (B* freely generates A*)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a subset B ⊂ A* freely generates A* (every word uniquely factors into elements of B), then the generating function of words in A* satisfies A*(λ) = (1 − B*(λ))^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Proposition 4.7.11: when B freely generates A*, the ordinary generating function for words formed from B has the simple algebraic relationship above. Use this when the combinatorial objects factor uniquely into prime blocks (examples and simple proofs provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique circular factorization (very pure monoids / UCF)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B* is 'very pure' (satisfies unique circular factorization, UCF) then there is a relation between the generating function of cyclic/conjugacy classes and B*: B*(λ) and the conjugacy-class counts g(n) satisfy B*(λ) = exp(sum_{n≥1} g(n) λ^n / n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 4.7.13: when UCF holds, the exponential/log relation gives the ordinary generating function for conjugacy classes (circular objects). The proposition also gives the equivalent formulation g(n) generating the exponent. Check UCF (see definition and examples) before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hadamard products for combining per-step generating functions
rubrics_metrics.description: When building objects by synchronizing contributions from several factor-classes at the same length m, use Hadamard products Fi1 * ··· * Fir to encode the per-length combination of weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the D_k constructions (products over compositions), matrix entries are Hadamard products of the Fi(x). The empty choice contributes the 'empty Hadamard product' J(x)=x/(1−x). Use Proposition 4.2.5 (Hadamard preserves rationality) to conclude rationality when each Fi is rational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling multi-factor products via state digraph D_k (epsilon-vectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: To expand products like (f1(n1)+…+fk(nk))(f1(n2)+…+fk(nk+1))… over compositions, build a digraph D_k whose vertices are k-bit vectors (ε1,…,εk−1) encoding which factors are 'available'; paths from (1,…,1) to (0,…,0) correspond to terms in the expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 4.7.20 gives an explicit construction of the 2^{k−1}×2^{k−1} matrix A_k: entries are Hadamard products determined by how ε and ε' change. Delete the sink/source rows/columns to form B_k, then the overall generating function F(x) = det B_k / det(I − A_k). This systematically converts such products into rational functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer-matrix for rook polynomials (nonattacking rooks)
rubrics_metrics.description: For counting placements of nonattacking rooks on B_n with restrictions up to distance k, build digraph D_k whose vertices are all possible placements of nonattacking rooks on the first k−1 rows; edges represent permissible overlaps, weighted by x^{#rooks in last row}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let A_k be adjacency matrix of D_k with these weights and set Q_k(λ)=det(I−λA_k). Then by Corollary 4.7.3 / formula (4.43) the rook-polynomial generating function R_n(x)λ^n satisfies R_n(x)λ^n = λ Q'_k(λ)/Q_k(λ) (suitably interpreting for small n). This reduces rook enumeration to determinant computations (examples: k=2, k=3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization method when prime-block decomposition exists (practical simplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: When combinatorial objects decompose as sequences/products of prime blocks (with a manageable list of primes), the factorization method often yields much simpler derivations and smaller computations than the transfer-matrix approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 4.7.11/4.7.13 to write generating functions as (1 − B*(λ))^{-1} or exp-sums as appropriate. The text repeatedly stresses that the factorization method can be 'extremely elegant and simple' compared with forming large adjacency matrices (examples: permutations, polyominoes, compositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for small-n exceptions / spurious values
rubrics_metrics.description: Values produced by the algebraic-generating-function formulas may give 'spurious' counts for very small n (e.g., g(1)=3, g(2)=5), so small n must be interpreted or corrected separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 4.7.3 and related remarks note that for small values of n (never larger than a specified p1) the combinatorial expectation may fail. Remedy by computing/adjusting initial cases explicitly or treating exceptional configurations separately (examples throughout §4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvalues give closed forms and linear recurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: The eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A explain why many counting sequences have simple closed forms (linear combinations of eigenvalue powers) and satisfy linear recurrences with constant coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute eigenvalues of A to derive explicit formulas (Examples derive Fibonacci and Lucas sequences from small adjacency matrices) and to determine recurrence orders (degree of Q(λ)). Use characteristic polynomial roots to obtain α^n+β^n forms when eigenvalues are simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight assignment conventions and encoding combinatorial statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose edge/graph weights to encode the combinatorial statistic of interest (e.g., w(e)=1 for counting, x^{#rooks} for rook polynomials, product of letter-weights for words). The empty/no-choice transition is represented by J(x)=x/(1−x) in some constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what each weight records (length, number of pieces, number of rooks, etc.). In the D_k composition construction, edges picking no factors contribute J(x); edges picking several factors contribute the appropriate Hadamard product of their Fi(x). Consistent weight choices ensure F is a well-defined formal power series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality transfer: composing rational Fi implies rational F
rubrics_metrics.description: If each per-class generating function Fi(x) is rational, then the constructed global generating function F(x) (via Ak / Bk, Hadamard products, determinant formulas) is rational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Proposition 4.2.5 (Hadamard product preserves rationality) together with the determinant/transfer-matrix constructions. Use this to conclude rationality of many combinatorial generating functions once local pieces are rational.
